newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies slip after rumors.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mixed, pork bellies slip after rumors.

text.p: CME hog futures slipped to close mixed and pork belly futures fell from late morning highs after a rumor over South Korea pork tender failed to keep the market supported, traders said.

Both pork pits ran up for sharp gains on talk that South Korea would be tendering for pork or pork bellies, as well as on early short covering. However, demand lacked enough punch to penetrate technicial resistance and weak cash and prices fell back late, traders said.
"It may take more than a rumor to turn these markets around in the face of weak fundamentals," one trader said.

Dave Maher, analyst for Securities Corp of Iowa, said hog and belly futures hit buy stops on the advance prompted by the rumor, but values then retreated when new buyers were reluctant to take the market up through technical resistance.
"The December (hog) contract is still trading below the long term uptrend line that we established," Maher said.
He cited recent weakness in cash pork prices and live markets for added resistance.
Active pork movement Wednesday was also ignored, he said.
Traders said cash hog markets will likely remain weak into next week.
Maher noted that although the pork belly Relative Strength Index, RSI, was under 25 and indicated an oversold market, futures could still work lower. Grain RSI's were in the teens, he added.
The February contract fell to its lowest level since mid April while cash belly prices have declined to their lowest levels since February 28.
Belly futures were also pressured by seasonal weakness. More bellies are starting to go into storage as seasonal demand wanes, traders said.

Next week's U.S. Cold Storage report is expected to show October 1 frozen belly stocks in a range from 11.9 million to 13.7 million lbs. Stocks will rise from this level as product moves into storage while consumers turn their attention to other seasonal meats and poultry, analysts said.
Hog futures ended 0.650 cent a lb higher to 0.125 lower with December up 0.500 at 55.925 cents. Pork bellies closed 0.125 to 0.450 lower with February off 0.125 at 70.300 cents.
